canonical_question: Do standard mechanical polishing protocols (1200-2000 grit SiC paper followed by vibromet polishing) sufficiently remove surface deformation layers for high-resolution analysis without introducing artifacts?

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: Both papers acknowledge the use of standard mechanical polishing (SiC paper and/or vibromet) for High-Entropy Alloy (HEA) surface preparation but explicitly lack quantitative validation that the deformation layer has been fully removed or that no new artifacts were introduced.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: One study prepares samples for SEM and XRD using 1200 grit SiC paper but reports only the grit size without assessing scratch depth [d5ce1a425b7e1101]. The other study employs a slightly more refined protocol (2000-grit paper followed by vibromet polishing with colloidal silica) for contact angle measurements but similarly fails to confirm the removal of the deformation layer generated during initial processing [2d1e1663799af3a4].
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The adequacy of the preparation depends on the specific analytical technique required; the first case highlights potential risks for high-resolution XRD where scratch depth is critical, while the second case questions the integrity of surface energy measurements (contact angle) where deformation artifacts may distort results.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no direct contradictions between the papers; both agree that the sufficiency of their respective protocols regarding deformation layer removal is unconfirmed by the reported data.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence is characterized by negative findings; the papers provide no positive data supporting the removal of deformation layers, only stating that the necessary quantitative analysis was not performed [d5ce1a425b7e1101, 2d1e1663799af3a4].
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: There is a missing regime of quantitative surface damage analysis (e.g., scratch depth measurement, XRD line profile analysis, or TEM of the surface layer) to determine the exact depth of deformation introduced by SiC paper grinding and whether vibromet polishing effectively removes it.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: 1200 grit SiC paper introduces scratches deep enough to compromise high-resolution XRD, while the addition of vibromet polishing with colloidal silica is required but not guaranteed to remove deformation layers for sensitive surface property measurements like contact angle.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform cross-sectional SEM/TEM on samples prepared with both 1200 grit SiC alone and 2000 grit + vibromet protocols to measure the depth of the plastically deformed zone versus the removal depth of the mechanical polishing steps.
